## Result

Vendor the complete fixed Asterinas v0.19.0 kernel (`c4b7ed575b7b32773475b194d2ad41fb6d03765b`, original tree `96605cf64aeae2d34f29b97e85eff9315fe10a8e`) at `kernel/asterinas/`, preserving licenses and documentation. Build through upstream `make kernel` / `make run_kernel` using nightly-2026-07-21 and a small BusyBox initramfs. The native profile uses x86_64 q35/TCG, CPU max, 1 vCPU, 512 MiB, explicit SeaBIOS, serial and debug exit, without an installation ISO.

This revision hardens host/build tooling: pass a private connected monitor FD to QEMU, preserve named-scheme inheritance, normalize the finite Cargo CLI, hold runner ownership through group cleanup, keep capture helpers in the outer cleanup group, and archive files through verified descriptor identities. It adds reproducible same-Linux-ELF diagnostic guests and cancellation of their directly owned QEMU children. A05/A06 kernel core and OSTD sources are unchanged; the project root README remains 0 bytes.

Latest actual main `99924da27531876d7c383d490175d06d8f200856` was incorporated without local conflicts after the prior A03 control merge. The added original A05 host wire/ENOTTY smoke passed; it does not exercise an Asterinas driver. Fixed inputs remain118 and no kernel guest counts were rerun or upgraded for the main-only merge. [Final sync evidence](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/blob/agents/A01-asterinas-boot/support/build/evidence/2026-10-16-review-main-sync/REPORT.md). A00 retains the main integration decision.

## Actual validation and limits

| Check | Measured result |
| --- | --- |
| Complete Rust kernel build/debug boot at `f473a2cc` | GDB hits `__ostd_main`, verifies 32 live bytes against both ELFs, detaches; full minimal initramfs boot passes, QEMU raw33 |
| Native TCP/GDB capture profile at `f473a2cc` | One full run: 22/22, 0 failed/blocked, 1 explicit VMX soft skip; 11 real guests raw33 |
| Later capture cleanup at `349a28ff` | Five host lifecycle checks, recorder35 and capture4 in each Python mode; separate actual coverage guest 1/1, raw33, 2,094,456 bytes, 5,696 LLVM functions. No later full22 rerun claimed |
| OSDK host tests | 38 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored; ignored real-QEMU transport probe separately passes, with no kernel loaded |
| Archive/Cargo/runner | Archive20 and Cargo13 per Python mode, 673 old files byte-verified, four real pinned-Cargo commands; runner10 plus original timeout1 per mode, profile7 |
| Original A04 sequential28 suite | Fails: 180s timeout after 8 matches and one completed failure |
| Fresh-guest A04 diagnostic at `d85b1e09` | 24 exact matches, 2 fd_limit completed failures, 2 SCM_RIGHTS timeouts /28; driver2. Four additional unported Python/Tokio cases are outside28 |
| Later diagnostic cancellation at `3db0aa8a` | Two real SCM signal checks: CLI143/130, owned pidfd exit, direct-child reap, queued case skipped. Focused3: 1 match/1 completed failure/1 timeout. No full28 rerun |
| Main merge and source integrity | 21 real host control tests passed; 118 fixed inputs verified; empty root README |

Retained failures include default UNIX OSDK20/22 (AF_UNIX EPERM), both TCP-v1 coverage pilots, old cleanup negative controls, and the original A04 suite. Earlier OSTD/aster-core362 reported passes include3 soft skips (359 exercised lower bound); these were not rerun in this phase. No SMP/VMX/EPT, full upstream userspace/device, HOS2, Hepta W1, block persistence or production-release claim.

## Build, handoff and evidence

```sh
support/build/prepare-host.sh --apt
support/build/kernel.sh kernel
support/build/kernel.sh run_kernel
python3 -I support/build/debug/run.py --output NEW_KERNEL_DEBUG_DIR
python3 -I support/build/osdk-integration/run.py --local-tcp --coverage-gdb --output NEW_TCP_CAPTURE_DIR
```

A05 interfaces: `kernel/core/src/process/process/mod.rs` (`Process`), `kernel/core/src/syscall/ioctl.rs`, and `kernel/core/src/fs/file/file_handle.rs` (`FileLike::ioctl`). A06 scheduler: `kernel/core/src/sched/sched_class/`. These paths are relative to `kernel/asterinas/`; core modifications remain with their owners.

Actionable core blockers: accepting RLIMIT_NOFILE=32 still permits256 opens; SCM_RIGHTS receive leaves CLOEXEC unset at the upstream `FileMessage::write_to` TODO, so the test child exits before its ACK and the parent times out. The same pinned static ELFs pass on the original Linux host. See the exact observation/inference boundaries and owner reproduction commands in the report.

[Full report and A00/A05/A06 handoff](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/blob/agents/A01-asterinas-boot/support/build/evidence/2026-10-16-review/REPORT.md) contains commands, selected environment, source/ELF/initramfs/firmware SHA256, exact QEMU arguments, complete serial/GDB logs, historical failed attempts and hash-indexed compressed payloads. [Diagnostic entry](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/blob/agents/A01-asterinas-boot/support/build/linux-guest/README.md) includes source/rootfs restoration and focused reproduction. Runtime Git dirty state and post-hoc byte bindings are explicit. Snapshot/path replacement anomalies and the generated-manifest protective refusal remain recorded; no service changes or overwrite bypass were used.

All267 archived files and the lock were verified from immutable Git index objects before the evidence commit. Compressed payloads retain verified member indices; `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` checks the final archive. Raw serial CRLF and original patch bytes are preserved.

comments.body: A00 new targeted review of **new** PR #22 OSDK TCP-monitor code at commit `54356654b0c88c1b0bec85cfdb4d7911839c6a3e` (separate from existing archive/Cargo adapter findings): `MonitorEndpoint::Tcp` binds an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` TCP listener and configures QEMU `-monitor tcp:<addr>,server=off`, but `try_connect()` unconditionally accepts **the first connecting local process** without authenticating that it is the spawned QEMU instance. A concurrent local process can connect before QEMU and become the OSDK monitor stream, supply fake HMP responses, or prevent the real monitor handshake. Loopback prevents remote network exposure but is **not an OS-user identity or QEMU provenance check**. The old temporary UNIX socket had filesystem ownership/permission semantics that are absent for TCP. Please keep TCP explicitly non-production/test-host-only unless you prove the trust boundary; add an adversarial two-client test (unauthorized local client connects first; OSDK must reject it rather than consume it as QEMU), plus a real q35/TCG smoke showing the legitimate connection, effective QEMU PID/provenance and timeout/failure classification. Avoid treating a successful `TcpStream` accept or monitor bytes as proof of a guest boot; tie verdict to full serial, artifact digests and raw QEMU exit as already required. Also preserve the default Unix path and do not weaken HOS2/Hepta pins. Existing 20/22 native OSDK case results and queued CI are not full pass; do not merge this large PR yet.
